goal: Lets a bitcoin-node process expose its Chain interface over an IPC socket, so wallet and other client code can run in a separate process and talk to a running node.
Serves as the shared plumbing that unblocks running the wallet (and other clients like GUI or external tools) out-of-process.

categories.name: ipc
why: P1 because this is the core interface wrapper needed to run the wallet, and eventually the GUI, as separate processes, the stated goal of the process-separation project.
It already has real external consumers (a Rust BDK wallet PoC, an Electrs-over-IPC PoC, and a live tracing dashboard), demonstrating concrete demand beyond Bitcoin Core itself.
It is the direct base for #10102, #19460, and #19461, so its merge state has a multiplying effect on other IPC work.

result.summary: This PR adds a Cap'n Proto wrapper that exposes Bitcoin Core's interfaces::Chain interface over an IPC socket, letting an external process (most notably a separated wallet process) call Chain methods on a running bitcoin-node. It bundles a Handler interface wrapper, generic capnp serialization helpers for util::Result/Expected and other types, and a large squashed update of the libmultiprocess subtree (CI, build, and correctness fixes). It also exposes the Chain interface directly for experimentation and adds small annotations to non-IPC structs (FeeCalculation, JSONRPCRequest) reminding maintainers to keep the capnp mirror in sync.
result.problem: External processes (a separated wallet, GUI, or third-party tools like block explorers, alternative wallets, or monitoring tools) currently cannot interact with a running bitcoin-node's Chain interface without linking into node internals; this PR gives them a defined IPC surface. It is a direct prerequisite for the long-standing goal of running the wallet in its own process (#10102).

open_concerns: zaidmstrr (2026-09-09) reports the node aborts with an assertion failure when getBlockHash is called with a height above the tip — unanswered as of the latest signals.

willcl-ark and ryanofsky discussed several places where malformed IPC input (null tx pointers, out-of-range enums) can crash the node; author acknowledges these as real but says they can't all be fixed in this PR and some already have tracked issues (libmultiprocess#219).

Sjors raised a broader design question in a separate issue (#34981) about whether shipping capnp files for this complete interface is the right approach, explicitly to avoid derailing this PR's code review.
resolved_concerns: l0rinc's large batch of schema-correctness findings (missing fields, 32/64-bit mismatches, bool-vs-int mismatches, stale names) were fixed in the 2025-12-12 push.
cbergqvist's early nits on value.has_value() vs operator bool and a stray include were resolved via explanation and a fix respectively.
Several silent-conflict build breakages from parallel PRs (#32438, #32862, #33169, #34568, #34075, etc.) were fixed via repeated rebases.

result.card: This PR adds the Cap'n Proto wrapper that exposes Bitcoin Core's interfaces::Chain over an IPC socket, letting an out-of-process client (most notably a future separated wallet process) call into a running bitcoin-node. It is explicitly the dependency base for #10102 (multiprocess wallet), #19460, and #19461, making it foundational to the process-separation project. Real external consumers already exist: a Rust BDK wallet PoC and tested ACK from darosior, an Electrs-over-IPC PoC and a live node dashboard from Sjors and willcl-ark, both giving concept/tested support. The PR has been open since February 2024 with 32 force pushes and extensive review (l0rinc's schema-correctness pass was fully addressed in December 2025), but testers keep finding crashes on malformed or edge-case input, most recently zaidmstrr's 2026-09-09 report of a node abort on an out-of-range getBlockHash call, which is unanswered as of the latest signals. Author treats most such crashes as known and tracked separately (e.g. libmultiprocess#219) rather than blocking, but the newest one is still open.
